title: Relative velocity in 2D and river-crossing decomposition

authority_basis.claim_scope: Pinned PR383 source defines 2D relative velocity by vector subtraction and river-crossing time/drift by perpendicular and parallel velocity components.

concepts.statement: The velocity of A relative to B is the vector difference of their velocities in the same reference frame; in river crossing, the perpendicular component controls crossing time while the parallel component controls drift.
concepts.why_required: It separates frame-relative motion from scalar speed comparison and keeps crossing duration distinct from downstream drift.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Relative velocities can be added with the wrong sign, or river drift can be confused with the component that determines crossing time.

symbols.name: velocity of A relative to B
velocity of A in common ground frame
velocity of B in common ground frame

conditions: Speeds are much less than c
v_A_ground and v_B_ground are expressed in the same frame
River width is measured perpendicular to the banks
The perpendicular velocity component is nonzero
Parallel and perpendicular components refer to the same river-crossing event

model_conditions.condition: Relative velocity is evaluated under the source-declared Galilean regime with speeds much less than c.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The source relation uses ordinary vector subtraction between velocities in a common frame.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The source-declared relative-velocity relation is outside its stated validity condition.

model_conditions.condition: Crossing duration is computed from the component perpendicular to the banks, while the parallel component contributes downstream drift.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The pinned source explicitly separates perpendicular crossing progress from parallel river drift.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Using resultant speed for crossing time conflates crossing progress with downstream drift.

representations.semantic_geometry: A river-bank diagram shows river velocity, boat velocity relative to water, resultant ground velocity, river width, and bank-parallel/perpendicular directions as one vector-triangle model.
must_not_imply: the component parallel to the bank determines crossing time
relative velocities may be combined as unsigned scalar speeds
representations.verification_method: Check the relative-velocity vector relation component-wise, compute crossing time from the perpendicular component, and compute drift from the parallel component over that same time.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Decompose the boat velocity into components parallel and perpendicular to the river bank while preserving the vector-relative-velocity relation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Crossing and drift calculations can use the resultant speed or the wrong component.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Compute crossing time from river width divided by the velocity component perpendicular to the bank.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Parallel drift can be incorrectly allowed to change the time needed to reach the opposite bank.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Compute downstream drift from the parallel velocity component multiplied by the crossing time.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The river-current effect can be confused with the perpendicular crossing component.

required_transformations.description: Translate the physical relative-motion scenario into a vector relation with explicit bank-parallel and bank-perpendicular components.
Use the perpendicular component for crossing time and the parallel component with that same time for downstream drift.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: A river current parallel to the bank necessarily increases the time required to cross directly to the opposite bank.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Downstream drift changes the visible path length and can be confused with progress across the river.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A river velocity purely parallel to the bank has zero projection on the perpendicular crossing axis.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use the river-boat vector diagram with explicit parallel and perpendicular axes, keeping drift and crossing progress on separate components.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Compute crossing time strictly from the velocity component perpendicular to the banks; use the parallel component only for drift.
misconceptions.verification: Recompute t_cross from d/v_perpendicular and confirm that changing only v_parallel changes x_drift but not t_cross.

problem_families.name: Shortest time versus shortest path river crossing
problem_families.first_technical_move: Resolve the boat and river velocities in bank-parallel and bank-perpendicular directions before computing time or drift.
fatal_errors: adding relative velocities as unsigned speeds
using resultant speed for crossing time
accepting an impossible heading requiring a component larger than the boat speed

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the relative-velocity subtraction invariant so addition can replace v_A - v_B.
